outcome.headline: Novakai Canvas now explains agent work with evidence, not transcript prose.
outcome.summary: A real Codex session now compiles into a visual before-to-after work report. It names the files and modules changed, records decisions and resolved problems, links delivered artifacts, and keeps repository-executed proof separate from agent claims.

changes.title: Turn work-session reporting into a host-neutral capability
changes.why: Canvas and standalone HTML need one trustworthy report authority instead of two renderers inventing their own story.
changes.before: Session facts, report policy, and rendered content had no shared immutable domain contract.
changes.after: WorkSession, WorkReceipt, ReportDraft, and AcceptedReport form one deterministic capability with stable IDs and acceptance gates.

changes.title: Import the actual Codex session through one strict adapter
changes.why: A useful report must describe the genuine work session while failing closed on unknown or malformed source records.
changes.before: The POC could prove its pipeline with a small fixture but could not safely normalize the changing live Codex JSONL shape.
changes.after: An explicitly selected real session is classified, normalized, source-digested, and rejected when identity or supported content is uncertain.

changes.title: Give agents a source-bound end-session receipt
changes.why: Agents need a compact structured handoff that creates useful narrative without being allowed to certify its own claims.
changes.before: Repository receipts could prove changed areas, but the human-facing explanation remained generic and omitted why, before-to-after, and resolved problems.
changes.after: The agent supplies Outcome, Changes, Decisions, Problems, Artifacts, and Remaining work; each change names files, module, reason, before, and after, while Proof is structurally impossible.

changes.title: Promote one Evidence Wall inside Canvas
changes.why: The report should answer what changed and what exists now at a glance, without forcing the reader through transcript prose.
changes.before: Three comparison variants and a prototype switcher made the POC itself the main thing the user had to understand.
changes.after: One stable report route leads with outcome, concrete accepted receipts, repository proof, the module map, and remaining work; the ordinary architecture canvas remains unchanged.

changes.title: Render the same accepted revision as immutable standalone HTML
changes.why: The reporting capability is only genuinely reusable if a second host can render the accepted projection without Canvas or React.
changes.before: The visual report was coupled to the application host and had no independently verifiable artifact.
changes.after: One deterministic renderer produces immutable HTML whose digest, source, receipts, projection, and evidence commit are verified at the publication boundary.

decisions.title: Treat reporting as one Canvas mode, not the Canvas redesign
decisions.rationale: This POC proves a Work Session Report capability inside the existing application. It does not propose global navigation, a new architecture editor, or the final visual language for every future Canvas mode.

decisions.title: Keep agent claims separate from acceptance proof
decisions.rationale: The brief may explain work but cannot author proof. Final generation executes npm run check inside the repository, binds its output to the evidence receipts, and refuses completion when proof fails.

decisions.title: Promote the Evidence Wall and delete the comparison variants
decisions.rationale: Variant C made delivered artifacts and proof primary. A, B, the switcher, prototype route, keyboard cycling, and losing tests were deleted instead of retained as permanent prototype debris.

decisions.title: Stop at the usefulness gate before building a reporting platform
decisions.rationale: The next decision is whether reports from three different real sessions remove the need to read transcripts. Navigation, report libraries, live streaming, generic composition, and a second visual product remain deliberately unbuilt.

problems.problem: The first real report was technically true but too generic to replace reading the session transcript.
problems.resolution: A versioned evidence-led projection now publishes the agent-authored change story and artifacts while retaining repository receipts and executed proof as separate authority.

problems.problem: Live Codex sessions contained current runtime record shapes that the original parser did not classify.
problems.resolution: The source adapter was expanded with an explicit current-format contract and tests; genuinely unsupported content still fails closed instead of being silently ignored.

problems.problem: A report generated from dirty or ambiguous repository state could make a true test result appear to prove different code.
problems.resolution: Final generation requires a named clean evidence commit, records its tree, rejects changed source after that commit, and writes only publication artifacts afterward.

artifacts.title: Stable Evidence Wall in Novakai Canvas
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: A production report route that visually leads with the session outcome, concrete changed work, delivered artifacts, important decisions, and repository-owned proof.

artifacts.title: Real Codex session reporting pipeline
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: A command that imports a selected Codex JSONL session, binds structured claims to it, derives repository evidence, runs the acceptance gate, and publishes one accepted revision.

artifacts.title: Agent end-session receipt contract
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: A small source-bound JSON protocol for Outcome, Changes, Decisions, Problems, Artifacts, and Remaining work. Agent-supplied proof is rejected.

artifacts.title: Independent immutable HTML report
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: A shareable no-React rendering of the exact accepted public projection, with a deterministic byte digest and historical v1 pages left untouched.

artifacts.title: Visual operating handover
artifacts.whatYouHaveNow: One HTML handover that shows the delivered pipeline, protocol boundary, exact report identities, verified desktop/mobile views, operating commands, assumptions, and deliberately unbuilt scope.

remainingWork.label: Use this exact reporting workflow on three genuine sessions before building navigation, a report library, or another visual type
